title: What color is a season?
hint: Choose a color family for each season
say: Welcome to Seasons in Color. Today we are trying a popular color practice: one small landscape, shown in spring, summer, autumn, and winter. Tap a color, then place it into the season it matches. There is no single perfect answer.

title: Prepare your paint table
hint: Watch each material light up, then check your own table
say: Before we paint, check your table. First, choose your paint. Gouache, watercolor, or acrylic paint are all welcome for this exercise. Next, prepare watercolor or mixed-media paper. You will also need a few paint brushes, a cup of clean water for rinsing, and a paper towel or cloth for cleaning and controlling your brush. The teacher uses gouache, while Rainy uses watercolor. One is not better than the other.

title: A real classroom color experiment
hint: Two paint sets, one shared practice
say: This exercise was painted together in a real class with a student named Rainy. The teacher uses gouache, and Rainy uses watercolor. Their results do not need to look the same, and yours does not need to match either one. We are practicing color, atmosphere, and feeling.

title: Spring · a flowering wash
mix: Rose + a touch of violet + plenty of water
hint: Keep the wash transparent. Let the paper glow.
say: First, build the spring atmosphere. The teacher starts with rose, adds a touch of violet, and uses plenty of water. Keep the layer transparent. Let the white paper shine through the pink wash.

title: Summer · a fresh green wash
mix: Lemon yellow + yellow-green + plenty of water
hint: Let yellow keep this green light and fresh.
say: For summer, begin with lemon yellow and move toward yellow-green. Keep yellow visible so the green feels fresh and full of light. Use water to spread the color softly.

title: Autumn · a golden wash
mix: Golden yellow + a little orange + water
hint: Warm the paper without making it heavy.
say: Now warm the autumn panel with golden yellow and a little orange. This first layer should feel sunny and light. Do not make it too dark yet; deeper autumn color will come later.

title: Winter · a pale blue wash
mix: Cerulean blue + a little deep blue + plenty of water
hint: Leave breathing room and quiet light.
say: For winter, use a pale cerulean blue with a small amount of deeper blue. Add plenty of water. Leave quiet spaces and light paper so the air feels open and cold.

title: Spring · draw the tree rhythm
mix: Rose-violet darkened with an earthy brown
hint: Branch upward with a few confident lines.
say: Now add structure. In spring, mix rose-violet with an earthy brown for the trunks and branches. Use a few confident lines, and let the branches reach upward through the pink atmosphere.

title: Summer · plant the trunks
mix: Earth brown cooled with a small green note
hint: Let the trunk sit inside the green atmosphere.
say: For the summer trees, cool the brown with a small green note. Place the trunks inside the yellow-green world. Keep the branches simple; the full canopy will come next.

title: Autumn · warm the branches
mix: Warm brown built from orange and red
hint: Use warm structure against the golden ground.
say: In autumn, build a warm brown from orange, red, and earth color. These warmer trunks belong naturally inside the golden background. Change the pressure of your brush to make thick and thin branches.

title: Winter · make the branches crisp
mix: Deep blue-violet, darkened only where needed
hint: Winter branches can be spare, dark, and clear.
say: For winter branches, mix deep blue and violet, then darken only where you need it. Winter trees can be spare, crisp, and clear. Leave more empty sky between the branches.

title: Summer · build a full canopy
mix: Layer several neighboring greens; keep small gaps of light
hint: Dab, overlap, and allow the greens to vary.
say: Now fill the summer canopy with neighboring greens: lemon yellow, yellow-green, leaf green, and blue-green. Dab and overlap the colors, but keep small gaps of light so the tree still feels alive.

title: Autumn · turn leaves toward gold
hint: Use a family of warm colors, not one flat orange.
say: Turn the autumn leaves from golden yellow to orange, then toward red-brown. Use a family of warm colors instead of one flat orange. Let each layer show through the next.

title: Winter · cool the earth and air
mix: Blue neighbors diluted into soft, cold layers
hint: The quiet paper is part of the winter palette.
say: Cool the winter ground and air with diluted cerulean, deep blue, and violet. The untouched paper is also part of this palette. Quiet light helps winter feel spacious.

title: Spring · return with blossom color
mix: Rose and violet blossoms over a soft green ground
hint: Finish with lively marks. Do not cover every first wash.
say: Return to spring with rose and violet blossoms over a soft green ground. Use lively dabs and small marks. Keep some of the first wash visible, so the painting stays light and fresh.

title: Can you feel four different seasons?
hint: Your colors do not need to match ours
say: Step back and compare all four panels. Your colors do not need to match ours. If each panel carries a different weather, temperature, or feeling, your Four Seasons color experiment is working.
